title: Pairing symmetry and superconductivity from long-range Coulomb interactions in the extended t-t'-t''-Jz model for cuprates
abstract: We investigate the pairing symmetry of the ground-state phase diagram of an extended two-dimensional $t$-$t'$-$t''$-$J_z$ model, in which the first-, second-, and third-nearest neighbor electron hopping terms ($t,t'$ and $t''$) and an anisotropic Ising-like antiferromagnetic interaction $J_z$ are treated on the same framework. We find that the dominant pairing symmetry depends sensitively on the sign and magnitude of the hopping parameters $t'$ and $t''$, showing pure $p$-wave, pure $d$-wave, or coexisting pairing channels, highlighting the decisive role of these terms. We further explore the role of the long-range and short-range repulsive interactions in the formation of pairs and analyze the specific case of hole-doped cuprates. Our results indicate that repulsive interactions favors hole pair escaping of the stripe domains. Furthermore, pairing correlation calculations strongly suggest that repulsive Coulomb interactions drive reentrant superconducting behavior at experimentally observed underdoped regime ($δ\approx0.07$ to $0.15$), as in Neodymium-based cuprates.
summary: This paper models cuprate superconductivity using an extended $t-t'-t''-J_z$ Hamiltonian that includes long-range Coulomb repulsion. The study finds that the pairing symmetry depends critically on hopping parameters and demonstrates that repulsive interactions can stabilize reentrant superconductivity in the underdoped regime. The methodology combines advanced quantum many-body techniques with symmetry analysis to diagnose superconducting order.
main_problem: The study investigates the pairing symmetry and superconducting behavior in cuprate superconductors, addressing the limitations of existing models in describing superconductivity across the full doping range.
main_result: The pairing symmetry is highly sensitive to the hopping parameters ($t', t''$), and repulsive Coulomb interactions are shown to drive reentrant superconducting behavior in the underdoped regime, consistent with experimental observations.
method: The authors use theoretical calculations on an extended two-dimensional $t-t'-t''-J_z$ model, employing techniques like the truncated Lanczos method and symmetry analysis based on the $	ext{D}_4$ point group.
model_or_system: The system is the extended two-dimensional $t-t'-t''-J_z$ model, which incorporates nearest, second, and third-nearest neighbor hopping terms ($t, t', t''$), an Ising-like antiferromagnetic interaction ($J_z$), and long-range Coulomb repulsive interactions ($H_V$).
key_observables: Pairing symmetry (p-wave, d-wave, or coexisting), pair-pair correlation function $P_{xx}(|r|)$, and the superconducting phase diagram ($\delta$ vs. $V$).
important_parameters: Hopping parameters ($t', t''$), doping level ($\delta$), and the strength of repulsive interactions ($V$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses the large-$U$ limit of the Hubbard model, approximates the spin exchange with an Ising term ($H_{Jz}$), and utilizes the Clifford torus distance metric for long-range interactions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate high-symmetry two-hole configurations and show the decay of the pair-pair correlation function $P_{xx}(|r|)$, confirming long-range order for superconducting states. A phase diagram maps reentrant superconductivity based on doping and repulsion.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian components, determines the ground state symmetry using group theory, diagnoses superconductivity via correlation functions, and finally maps out the superconducting phase diagram showing reentrant behavior.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding high-Tc superconductivity by incorporating multiple hopping terms and long-range Coulomb repulsion, which is a key challenge in strongly correlated electron theory.
